summary: Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 2010) under John Powers, and studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang as well as with several traditional Tibetan teachers.
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 2002 to 2018.

Peter Koret specializes in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford and Tokyo, he taught at the University of Tasmania and Kyoto University before serving at the University of Cambridge (~1985–2017) and Robinson College.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993). He held academic posts at the University of Giessen (~1995–2002), University of Düsseldorf (~2002–2004), and University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, also studying with Shrinarayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986), and taught Nicolas Revire.

Peter Moran works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and earned a PhD from the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, also training under traditional Tibetan teachers including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Peter N. Gregory is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD from Harvard (1981). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Kuroda Institute, Komazawa University, and Smith College (attested 2005).

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who earned his PhD under Paul Hacker at Münster and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held positions at the Göttingen Academy (1978), Humboldt University (2001), and Bonn (2001).

Peter Skilling is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and several visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of Indology, classical art, and archaeology. Educated at Clare College, Cambridge, he held posts at Reading and the Courtauld before becoming Director of the Classical Art Research Centre and Associate Professor at Oxford in 2011.

Peter Zieme specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies and linguistics. Educated at Humboldt University, he worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences, Institut für Orientforschung, Berlin-Brandenburg Academy, and Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer is a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Groningen and Utrecht. He held professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, and Pennsylvania, and served as Director at the Max Planck Institute (~2008–2021).

Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied in Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and A. W. Schlegel. He habilitated at Königsberg (~1825–1826) and served there as professor of oriental literature from 1825.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat, Tübingen, and Jena. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Giessen (~1883–1884), where he served as an associate professor from 1886 to 1896.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinz Bechert (~1985–1991) and served as a research fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz (attested 2013, 2016).

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has been affiliated with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, the University of Munich, and the International Consortium for Research in the Humanities.
